passages.s: Individuals of the same species often present, as is known to every one, great differences of structure, independently of variation, as in the two sexes of various animals, in the two or three castes of sterile females or workers among insects, and in the immature and larval states of many of the lower animals.

tr.fr: Les individus d'une même espèce présentent souvent, comme chacun le sait, de grandes différences de structure, indépendamment de la variation, comme dans les deux sexes de divers animaux, dans les deux ou trois castes de femelles stériles ou ouvrières parmi les insectes, et dans les états immatures et larvaires de beaucoup d'animaux inférieurs.

passages.s: It may be well here to remark that with all beings there must be much fortuitous destruction, which can have little or no influence on the course of natural selection.

tr.fr: Il convient peut-être ici de remarquer que tous les êtres doivent subir de nombreuses destructions fortuites, qui peuvent avoir peu ou pas d'influence sur le cours de la sélection naturelle.

passages.s: Whether natural selection has really thus acted in adapting the various forms of life to their several conditions and stations, must be judged by the general tenour and balance of evidence given in the following chapters.

tr.fr: La teneur générale et l'équilibre des preuves données dans les chapitres suivants doivent déterminer si la sélection naturelle a réellement agi ainsi en adaptant les diverses formes de vie à leurs diverses conditions et stations.

passages.s: An extremely wide flank-membrane stretches from the corners of the jaw to the tail, and includes the limbs with the elongated fingers.

tr.fr: Une membrane latérale extrêmement large s'étend des coins de la mâchoire jusqu'à la queue et comprend les membres aux doigts allongés.

passages.s: Mivart’s objections, it may be well to explain once again how natural selection will act in all ordinary cases.

tr.fr: Mivart, il serait peut-être bon d’expliquer une fois de plus comment la sélection naturelle agira dans tous les cas ordinaires.

passages.s: A little dose of judgment or reason, as Pierre Huber expresses it, often comes into play, even with animals low in the scale of nature.

tr.fr: Une petite dose de jugement ou de raison, comme l'exprime Pierre Huber, entre souvent en jeu, même avec des animaux bas à l'échelle de la nature.

passages.s: Eyton, who raised two hybrids from the same parents, but from different hatches; and from these two birds he raised no less than eight hybrids (grandchildren of the pure geese) from one nest.

tr.fr: Eyton, qui a élevé deux hybrides issus des mêmes parents, mais issus de couvées différentes ;  et de ces deux oiseaux il n'éleva pas moins de huit hybrides (petits-enfants des oies pures) d'un même nid.

passages.s: Although each formation may mark a very long lapse of years, each probably is short compared with the period requisite to change one species into another.

tr.fr: Bien que chaque formation puisse marquer un laps de temps très long, chacune est probablement courte comparée à la période nécessaire pour transformer une espèce en une autre.

passages.s: We can understand how it is that dominant forms which spread widely and yield the greatest number of varieties tend to people the world with allied, but modified, descendants; and these will generally succeed in displacing the groups which are their inferiors in the struggle for existence.

tr.fr: Nous pouvons comprendre comment les formes dominantes qui se répandent largement et donnent le plus grand nombre de variétés tendent à peupler le monde de descendants alliés, mais modifiés ;  et ceux-ci réussiront généralement à évincer les groupes qui leur sont inférieurs dans la lutte pour l'existence.

passages.s: Even the uniform county of Cambridge has 847 plants, and the little island of Anglesea 764, but a few ferns and a few introduced plants are included in these numbers, and the comparison in some other respects is not quite fair.

tr.fr: Même le comté uniforme de Cambridge compte 847 plantes, et la petite île d'Anglesea 764, mais quelques fougères et quelques plantes introduites sont incluses dans ces chiffres, et la comparaison à certains autres égards n'est pas tout à fait juste.

passages.s: Yet all these organs, serving for such widely different purposes, are formed by infinitely numerous modifications of an upper lip, mandibles, and two pairs of maxillæ.

tr.fr: Cependant tous ces organes, servant à des usages si différents, sont formés par des modifications infinies d'une lèvre supérieure, de mandibules et de deux paires de maxillaires.

passages.s: As species have generally diverged in character during their long course of descent and modification, we can understand why it is that the more ancient forms, or early progenitors of each group, so often occupy a position in some degree intermediate between existing groups.

tr.fr: Comme les espèces ont généralement divergé dans leurs caractères au cours de leur longue descendance et de leurs modifications, nous pouvons comprendre pourquoi les formes les plus anciennes, ou les premiers ancêtres de chaque groupe, occupent si souvent une position intermédiaire dans une certaine mesure entre les groupes existants.

passages.s: Where this animal is abundant, it may be heard at all times of the day, and sometimes directly beneath one's feet.

tr.fr: Là où cet animal est abondant, on l'entend à tout moment de la journée, et parfois directement sous les pieds.

passages.s: The larger quadrupeds no doubt roam over wide tracts in search of it; and their food chiefly consists of underwood, which probably contains much nutriment in a small bulk.

tr.fr: Les plus gros quadrupèdes parcourent sans aucun doute de vastes étendues à sa recherche ;  et leur nourriture consiste principalement en sous-bois, qui contient probablement beaucoup de nutriments dans une petite quantité.

passages.s: Each is drawn by six bullocks, which are urged on by a goad at least twenty feet long: this is suspended from within the roof; for the wheel bullocks a smaller one is kept; and for the intermediate pair, a point projects at right angles from the middle of the long one.

tr.fr: Chacun est tiré par six bœufs, qui sont poussés par un aiguillon d'au moins vingt pieds de long : celui-ci est suspendu au dedans du toit ;  pour les bœufs de roue, on en garde un plus petit ;  et pour la paire intermédiaire, une pointe fait saillie à angle droit à partir du milieu de la paire longue.

passages.s: If a man who is poor commits murder and is taken, he will be imprisoned, and perhaps even shot; but if he is rich and has friends, he may rely on it no very severe consequence will ensue.

tr.fr: Si un homme pauvre commet un meurtre et est arrêté, il sera emprisonné et peut-être même fusillé ; mais s'il est riche et a des amis, il peut compter sur lui, sans que cela n'entraîne de conséquences très graves.

passages.s: The predominant colours are roan and iron-grey.

passages.s: If any present was designed for one canoe, and it fell near another, it was invariably given to the right owner.

passages.s: Before arriving there, the last land-locked basin had expanded into a great plain, which extended so far to the south, that the snowy summits of the more distant Andes were seen as if above the horizon of the sea.

passages.s: We steered northward along shore, but owing to thick weather did not reach Valdivia till the night of the 8th.

passages.s: Early in my school days a boy had a copy of the ‘Wonders of the World,’ which I often read, and disputed with other boys about the veracity of some of the statements; and I believe that this book first gave me a wish to travel in remote countries, which was ultimately fulfilled by the voyage of the “Beagle”.

I had never seen in those old days Licinus alive, which to an uneducated eye hardly differs from many of the black Carabidous beetles; but my sons found here a specimen, and I instantly recognised that it was new to me; yet I had not looked at a British beetle for the last twenty years.
Everything about which I thought or read was made to bear directly on what I had seen or was likely to see; and this habit of mind was continued during the five years of the voyage.
Formerly Milton’s ‘Paradise Lost’ had been my chief favourite, and in my excursions during the voyage of the “Beagle”, when I could take only a single volume, I always chose Milton.

The writing of this paper cost me four months; but I was so unwell when I received the proof-sheets that I was forced to leave them very badly and often obscurely expressed.

Formerly I used to think about my sentences before writing them down; but for several years I have found that it saves time to scribble in a vile hand whole pages as quickly as I possibly can, contracting half the words; and then correct deliberately.
